title: Where Dyes Learned Their Alphabets

features.name: vat-of-first-colours
features.desc-on-touch: Indigo so deep it holds itself like sky at midnight. The dye learns here that colour is a language older than words — you read it through your skin before your mind catches up.

features.name: madder-alphabet
features.desc-on-touch: Cloth hanging in orders of red. Each shade is a letter in the dye's own alphabet — statement, question, memory, longing. The archive records them like a dictionary of what warmth feels like.

features.name: cochineal-containment
features.desc-on-touch: The bug-deep reds stored in ceramic. Colour that came from insect-suffering, now teaching the archive what it means to carry pain in brightness.

features.name: saffron-cipher
features.desc-on-touch: Gold thread that cost more than comfort. The dye rare and precious, teaching that some alphabets demand scarcity to be read with proper reverence.

features.name: lichen-learning-wall
features.desc-on-touch: Stone stained by years of dye-runs. The lichen has learned to read the alphabet too — green on orange, yellow on grey. Two alphabets teaching each other.

inscription: the gallery where cloth first learned that colour is memory written in a language before memory

reverie.title: REVERIE — hands in the red vat
narr: You kneel beside her at the dye-vat, her hands deep
in madder-red. She teaches your hands to know by doing.
The colour stains you both — not washing out, becoming
part of the skin. She says: 'The dye is writing us now.'
You watch the cloth transform under her careful hands.
This is how archives are made: through touch, through time.
